memories.text: Dana prefers pnpm over npm for JavaScript projects.
The Lark API listens on port 8443 in production.
Dana's team deploys to production on Thursdays after the 2pm review.
The main database for Lark is PostgreSQL 16.
Dana is allergic to peanuts.
Dana's manager is Priya Raman.
The staging cluster runs in the eu-west-3 region.
Lark's frontend is written in Svelte.
Dana uses Neovim as her code editor.
The on-call rotation hands over every Monday at 9am.
Error tracking for Lark goes to Sentry.
Dana's cat is named Biscuit.
The Lark CI pipeline runs on Buildkite.
The test suite must finish in under 12 minutes.
Dana drinks oat milk flat whites.
The billing service uses Stripe for card payments.
Lark's search feature is backed by OpenSearch.
Dana's work laptop is a ThinkPad X1 Carbon.
The Lark mobile app is built with Flutter.
Feature flags are managed in LaunchDarkly.
The Lark design system is called Pebble.
Application logs are retained for 30 days.
Dana works on Lisbon time.
Lark's public docs are hosted on Mintlify.
The analytics warehouse is ClickHouse.
Dana wants commit messages written in the imperative mood.
The support inbox address is help@lark.example.
Dana's favorite programming language is Rust.
Product images are served from Cloudflare Images.
Customer data must stay inside the EU because of GDPR.
The auth service issues JWTs that expire after 15 minutes.
Dana's daughter Mia has swim practice on Wednesdays.
Lark's Python services use Poetry for dependency management.
The load balancer in front of Lark is HAProxy.
Dana prefers meetings that last 25 minutes.
Background jobs run on Sidekiq.
The Lark 2.0 launch is planned for March 12.
Dana's GitHub handle is dana-codes.
The Redis cache TTL is 300 seconds.
Dana is vegetarian.
The Slack channel for incidents is #lark-fire.
Lark is translated into English, Portuguese and Japanese.
Secrets are stored in HashiCorp Vault.
Dana's desk is on the 7th floor.
The Lark API rate limit is 600 requests per minute per key.
Transactional email is sent through Postmark.
Dana runs a 10k every Saturday morning.
The Node services use Prisma as their ORM.
The monorepo is built with Turborepo.
Dana expects code reviews to be done the same day.
Database backups run nightly at 02:00 UTC.
Production runs Kubernetes 1.31.
Dana dislikes long standup meetings.
The status page lives at status.lark.example.
Lark's mascot is a blue heron named Hugo.
Dana's sister lives in Porto.
Team video calls happen on Whereby.
The p95 latency target for search is 200 ms.
Dana's terminal app is WezTerm.
Lark's source code is released under MPL-2.0.
The staging database for Lark is MySQL 8.
Dana's brother prefers yarn for his JavaScript projects.
The internal admin API listens on port 7001.
The marketing website deploys on Fridays.
Priya's cat is named Pixel.
Search query logs are retained for 7 days.
The mobile app has a rate limit of 100 requests per minute.
The data team uses DuckDB for local analysis.
Dana's old personal laptop was a MacBook Air.
Mia's school is on Rua das Flores.
Change: the Lark API now listens on port 9443 in production.
Dana's team moved production deploys to Tuesdays.
Dana now reports to Tomas Lindqvist.
Dana switched her code editor to Zed.
The Lark CI pipeline moved to GitHub Actions.
Lark's search feature now runs on Typesense.
Feature flags moved to Unleash.
Application log retention was extended to 90 days.
Dana relocated and now works on Berlin time.
Auth JWTs now expire after 60 minutes.
Lark's Python services switched to uv for dependency management.
The Lark 2.0 launch moved to April 2.
Dana's desk moved to the 3rd floor.
The Lark API rate limit was raised to 1200 requests per minute per key.
Production Kubernetes was upgraded to 1.33.
